---
title: "Exercise 4: Building an analysis-ready first-IHD-event dataset"
format: html
execute:
  echo: true
---

## Learning goals

By the end of this exercise, you should be able to:

- link data with different units of observation;
- understand one-to-many joins;
- create broad and strict IHD event indicators;
- select a first qualifying IHD event;
- create a person-level dataset for later analysis.

## Load packages and data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

source(here("R", "01_helpers.R"))

cohort <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "cohort_baseline.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |> 
  mutate(baseline_date = ymd(baseline_date))

contacts <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "registry_contacts.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |> 
  mutate(
    admission_date = parse_mixed_date(admission_date_raw),
    discharge_date = parse_mixed_date(discharge_date_raw),
    contact_date = parse_mixed_date(contact_date_raw)
  )

diagnoses <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "registry_diagnoses.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |> 
  mutate(
    diagnosis_date = parse_mixed_date(diagnosis_date_raw),
    code_standardised = clean_code(diagnosis_code)
  )

lookup <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "icd_harmonisation_lookup.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

followup <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "death_followup.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |> 
  mutate(
    death_date = parse_mixed_date(death_date_raw),
    administrative_end_followup = ymd(administrative_end_followup_raw)
  )
```

## Task 1: Create a diagnosis-level event dataset

Join diagnosis data to contact data and the ICD lookup table.

```{r}
event_data <- diagnoses |> 
  left_join(
    contacts |> 
      select(
        contact_id,
        person_id,
        hospital,
        department,
        setting,
        admission_date,
        discharge_date,
        contact_date
      ),
    by = c("contact_id", "person_id")
  ) |> 
  left_join(
    lookup |> 
      select(
        coding_system,
        code_standardised,
        clinical_group,
        include_broad_ihd,
        include_strict_ihd
      ),
    by = c("coding_system", "code_standardised")
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    event_date = coalesce(admission_date, contact_date, diagnosis_date),
    broad_ihd = replace_na(include_broad_ihd, FALSE)
  )

event_data |> 
  arrange(person_id, event_date)
```

Questions:

1. What does one row represent in `event_data`?
2. Why does this dataset contain multiple rows per participant?
3. Why would it be incorrect to treat it as a person-level analysis dataset?

## Task 2: Create a strict phenotype

Create a strict inpatient-primary IHD indicator.

```{r}
event_data <- event_data |> 
  mutate(
    strict_ihd_inpatient = broad_ihd &
      setting == "Inpatient" &
      diagnosis_position == "Primary"
  )
```

Create a repeated outpatient IHD indicator.

```{r}
outpatient_counts <- event_data |> 
  filter(broad_ihd, setting == "Outpatient") |> 
  distinct(person_id, event_date) |> 
  count(person_id, name = "n_outpatient_ihd_dates")

event_data <- event_data |> 
  left_join(outpatient_counts, by = "person_id") |> 
  mutate(
    strict_ihd_outpatient = setting == "Outpatient" &
      replace_na(n_outpatient_ihd_dates, 0) >= 2,
    strict_ihd = strict_ihd_inpatient | strict_ihd_outpatient
  )
```

## Task 3: Identify possible prevalent IHD

Use registry records before baseline.

```{r}
prevalent_registry_ihd <- event_data |> 
  left_join(
    cohort |> 
      select(person_id, baseline_date),
    by = "person_id"
  ) |> 
  filter(
    broad_ihd,
    !is.na(event_date),
    event_date < baseline_date
  ) |> 
  distinct(person_id) |> 
  mutate(prevalent_registry_ihd = TRUE)

prevalent_registry_ihd
```

Discuss whether registry history alone is sufficient to identify all prevalent IHD.

## Task 4: Select first qualifying events after baseline

Create first broad and strict event dates after baseline.

```{r}
events_after_baseline <- event_data |> 
  left_join(
    cohort |> 
      select(person_id, baseline_date),
    by = "person_id"
  ) |> 
  filter(!is.na(event_date), event_date >= baseline_date)

first_broad_event <- events_after_baseline |> 
  filter(broad_ihd) |> 
  group_by(person_id) |> 
  slice_min(event_date, with_ties = FALSE) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  select(
    person_id,
    broad_first_ihd_date = event_date,
    broad_event_hospital = hospital,
    broad_event_setting = setting
  )

first_strict_event <- events_after_baseline |> 
  filter(strict_ihd) |> 
  group_by(person_id) |> 
  slice_min(event_date, with_ties = FALSE) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  select(
    person_id,
    strict_first_ihd_date = event_date,
    strict_event_hospital = hospital,
    strict_event_setting = setting
  )
```

## Task 5: Create a one-row-per-person dataset

```{r}
analysis_ready <- cohort |> 
  left_join(prevalent_registry_ihd, by = "person_id") |> 
  left_join(first_broad_event, by = "person_id") |> 
  left_join(first_strict_event, by = "person_id") |> 
  left_join(followup, by = "person_id") |> 
  mutate(
    prevalent_registry_ihd = replace_na(prevalent_registry_ihd, FALSE),
    censor_date = pmin(
      death_date,
      administrative_end_followup,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    broad_event = !is.na(broad_first_ihd_date) &
      broad_first_ihd_date <= censor_date,
    strict_event = !is.na(strict_first_ihd_date) &
      strict_first_ihd_date <= censor_date,
    broad_followup_days = as.numeric(
      coalesce(broad_first_ihd_date, censor_date) - baseline_date
    )
  )

analysis_ready
```

Check whether you have one row per participant.

```{r}
analysis_ready |> 
  count(person_id) |> 
  filter(n > 1)
```

## Reflection

1. How many people are classified as broad IHD events?
2. How many are classified as strict IHD events?
3. Which participants change classification?
4. What information has been lost when the dataset changes from diagnosis-level to person-level?
5. Which derivation decisions must be documented for reproducibility?
